newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia pay TV meets drama content goal-ABA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia pay TV meets drama content goal-ABA.

text.p: Australia's pay television industry have met the requirements of spending 10 percent of their annual programme expenditure on new local drama productions, the Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said.

"The majority of pay TV broadcasters and channel providers spent money as required on new Australian drama in the period ending 30, June 1996," ABA member Tim O'Keefe told the Australasian Cable and Satellite Television conference.
"The pay TV industry as a whole appears to have exceeded the 10 percent requirement for programme expenditure on drama channels," O'Keefe said.
The ABA is currently investigating local content rules for pay TV, starting with an evaluation of the effectiveness of the current 10 percent requirement.
The review is also looking into the feasibility of increasing the level of annual expenditure on new Australian drama programmes to 20 percent of programme expenditure.
